Name: Induction
Description: A single, mandatory session covering the theatre's history and culture, an overview of the committee and show proposal process, the code of conduct, and essential safety and emergency procedures. Baseline for all members; repeated annually as content changes.

Name: Get-in Brief
Description: Repeated at each get-in: safety and emergency reminders, follow HoD instructions, ask for help. Recorded as attendance, which doubles as get-in attendance tracking.

Name: Get-out Brief
Description: Repeated at each get-out: safety and emergency reminders, follow HoD instructions, ask for help. Recorded as attendance.

Name: First Aid
Description: External accredited certificate, for example the SU-run Emergency First Aid at Work. The system records the certificate and its own expiry date.
Notes: EXPANDED. Theatre target is at least one valid first-aider at every performance and workshop session.

Name: Fire Procedure
Description: Alarm points and sounds, evacuation routes and assembly point, extinguisher types and when not to fight a fire, show-stop and evacuation announcements, and roles during an evacuation (DM, backstage).
Notes: EXPANDED. Annual because procedures and building layout change.

Name: Manual Handling
Description: Safe lifting technique, team lifts and communication, moving awkward loads such as steeldeck, flats and pianos, when to use trucks or skates, and when to say no.
Notes: EXPANDED. Required before heavy work on get-ins.

Name: Ladder Safety and Working at Height
Description: A-frames, extension ladders and the Zarges: inspection before use, correct footing, three points of contact, working over other people, exclusion zones, and passing tools and equipment up and down.
Notes: EXPANDED. Required for any rigging or high-level work.

Name: Workshop Induction
Description: Mandatory for all workshop use. Safe use of basic hand tools such as drills and saws, workshop protocols, PPE, dust and noise, and emergency procedures.

Name: Powered Workshop Tools
Description: Extends the workshop induction to powered bench and free tools: chop saw, circular saw, jigsaw, sanders and pillar drill. Which tools members may use after sign-off, and which remain supervised or CWM-only.
Notes: NEW: subcommittee to confirm. Short refresh because these are the highest-risk items in the building.

Name: Risk Assessments
Description: How to write and review a risk assessment for a show, get-in or workshop activity: hazard identification, likelihood and severity, controls, and the sign-off flow with committee.
Notes: NEW: subcommittee to confirm. Aimed at producers, SMs and HoDs; feeds PROD-201.

Name: Set Construction Basics
Description: Flats: building, repairing, joining and bracing. Timber selection, basic joints, screws versus bolts versus staples, and preparing surfaces for paint. What the stock set pieces are and how they are stored.
Notes: NEW section: subcommittee to confirm.

Name: Building Decking
Description: Steeldeck: legs, bracing, handrails, safe assembly and stacking, safe working loads, and checking a build before it is stood on.
Notes: NEW section: subcommittee to confirm.

Name: Scenic Painting and Texturing
Description: Priming and base coats, blocking in, wood-graining and stone effects, texture with sawdust and filler, and keeping the paint store usable for the next show.
Notes: NEW section: subcommittee to confirm.

Name: Advanced Construction
Description: Load-bearing structures: treads and staircases, raised platforms and balustrades, trucks and castors, span rules, and when to ask the CWM. Anything an actor stands on above deck height goes through a certified builder or active supervision.
Notes: NEW section: subcommittee to confirm.

Name: Set Design
Description: Reading and drawing ground plans, model boxes, sightlines from the NNT's seating, designing within budget and buildability, the design deadline cycle, and collaborating with the director and CWM.
Notes: NEW section: subcommittee to confirm.

Name: Certified Set Designer
Description: Complete all Set and Workshop modules and design or build a show supervised. Signed off by the CWM. May then supervise Set and Workshop.
Notes: NEW section: subcommittee to confirm.

Name: Intro to Stage Management
Description: Base knowledge of the stage management team and its roles.

Name: Being a Stage Manager
Description: Fight calls, intimacy coordination, and running show week.

Name: Being an Assistant Stage Manager
Description: Props: sourcing, running and returning.

Name: Being a Deputy Stage Manager
Description: Calling a show.

Name: Intimacy and Fight Basics
Description: Running safe intimacy and fight calls: consent and check-ins, choreography discipline (never improvise contact), when the society must bring in an accredited external director, and safeguarding and reporting routes. This is coordination training, not choreography training: it certifies running calls, not staging violence.
Notes: NEW content naming the sheet's placeholder row: subcommittee to confirm. Expiry set at 24 months because practice and policy in this area moves.

Name: Certified Stage Manager
Description: Complete all Stage Management modules and hold any SM-team role on a show supervised. Signed off by a CSM. May then supervise SM teams.
Notes: Named by the ITM draft: subcommittee to confirm.

Name: Wardrobe Fundamentals
Description: Taking measurements, fitting etiquette and consent, costume care and laundry, the wardrobe store and stock system, hires and returns, and budgets for costume.
Notes: NEW section: subcommittee to confirm. Sign-off lead TBC.

Name: Sewing Basics
Description: Hand stitches, sewing machine setup and safe use, common repairs, hemming, and taking in or out.
Notes: NEW section: subcommittee to confirm.

Name: Hair and Makeup Basics
Description: Hygiene and allergy checks, base stage makeup for the NNT's lighting, ageing and character basics, and quick-change-friendly hair.
Notes: NEW section: subcommittee to confirm.

Name: Costume Design
Description: Period and character research, costume plots and quick-change planning, designing within budget and stock, and working with directors and actors' comfort.
Notes: NEW section: subcommittee to confirm.

Name: Making and Alterations
Description: Working from patterns, altering charity-shop and stock finds, and distressing and breaking down.
Notes: NEW section: subcommittee to confirm.

Name: Certified Costume Designer
Description: Complete all Costume modules and design a show supervised. Signed off by the costume lead. May then supervise Wardrobe.
Notes: NEW section: subcommittee to confirm. Sign-off lead TBC.

Name: Intro to Producing
Description: What a producer actually does at the NNT: the show lifecycle from proposal to get-out, assembling and supporting a team, the committee's role, and where to get help when it goes wrong.
Notes: NEW section: subcommittee to confirm. Sign-off lead TBC.

Name: Budgeting and Show Finance
Description: Setting and tracking a show budget, petty cash and reclaims, working with the Treasurer, and what happens when you overspend.
Notes: NEW section: subcommittee to confirm.

Name: Marketing Your Show
Description: Working with the Marketing team: poster and social deadlines, press and reviewers, photography calls, and archive requirements. Sits alongside ADMN-111, which is the delivering side.
Notes: NEW section: subcommittee to confirm.

Name: Rights and Licensing
Description: Securing performance rights, licensing bodies and typical timelines, what you may and may not cut or re-arrange, music licensing, and the no rights, no show rule.
Notes: NEW section: subcommittee to confirm.

Name: Production Management
Description: The production schedule, planning a get-in and get-out, risk assessments for the show, coordinating HoDs, and contingency planning.
Notes: NEW section: subcommittee to confirm.

Name: Certified Producer
Description: Complete all Producing modules and produce a show mentored by an experienced producer. Signed off by the producing lead. May then mentor new producers.
Notes: NEW section: subcommittee to confirm. Sign-off lead TBC.

Name: Front of House Management
Description: Managing reservations and tickets on the door, emergency procedures and the DM role, pre-show announcements, access needs and the access provision on show nights, and handling incidents and the end-of-night report.
Notes: EXPANDED; prerequisite NNT-001 added by the ITM draft. Annual because it feeds duty-manager eligibility and FOH procedure changes with the new box office.

Name: Selling Alcohol
Description: Committee only. Licence conditions, Challenge 25, refusing service, the refusals log, and closing the bar.
Notes: EXPANDED; prerequisite ADMN-101 added by the ITM draft. Annual, matching the FOH refresh.

Name: Box Office and Ticketing
Description: Using Proscenium as front-of-house or box-office staff: looking up and collecting reservations, the show-night screen and QR scanning, walk-up sales, comps and passes, and closing the night.
Notes: NEW: subcommittee to confirm. This is the training behind granting the proscenium FRONT_OF_HOUSE and BOX_OFFICE roles.

Name: Publicity and Marketing Basics
Description: Advertising through posters, social media and similar, and recording a show.

Name: Committee Operations and Governance
Description: Specialised training for elected committee members: duties, responsibilities, governance and welfare structures. Delivered to the incoming committee annually.

Name: Running a Workshop
Description: Teaching techniques, constructive feedback, and managing a workshop environment. Required for all members wishing to deliver training.

Name: Trainer
Description: Allows a member to run training sessions unsupervised: this certification is what unlocks logging a session in this system. Requires LEAD-301, delivering a workshop supervised, manual sign-off, and committee approval.
Notes: Proposed academic-year expiry flagged in the draft: trainer standing renews each year with a light-touch re-approval. Subcommittee may prefer never.
